t.SALICYLIC_ACID.agn: Classified in the EU as suspected of damaging fertility or the unborn child (CMR category 2). As a preservative the limit is 0.5% (Annex V, entry 3); for other purposes 3% in rinse-off hair products, 2% in most products, and 0.5% in body lotion, eye shadow, mascara, eyeliner, lipstick and roll-on deodorant (Annex III, entry 98). Not used in products for children under 3 (except shampoos, as a preservative), in oral products or in applications that can be inhaled.
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.eff.0: Classified in the EU for suspected reproductive toxicity (Repr. 2); the cosmetic limits rest on the SCCS finding these levels safe.
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.k3.0: EU priority list of potential endocrine disruptors (group B). On the 28-substance priority list that the European Commission drew up in 2019 for potential endocrine disruptors in cosmetics (substances suspected of possibly affecting the hormone system), in Group B. The assessment of part of this group is ongoing; the status of substances that have been concluded is stated separately. The list is not a ruling; it shows the order of assessment.
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.pw.0: In the EU it is not used in products for children under 3 (except shampoos, as a preservative).
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.pw.1: In the EU it is not used in products for children under 3 (except shampoos, as a preservative).
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.reg.0: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III, entry 98: Restricted substance: upper limits and conditions of use depend on the product type. CMR category 2 in the EU (suspected carcinogen/mutagen/reproductive toxicant).
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.reg.1: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex V, entry 3: Permitted preservative, with an upper limit.
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.summary: A beta hydroxy acid (BHA) used in acne and dandruff products.
t.SALICYLIC_ACID.what: Helps dead skin cells shed (keratolytic) and clears pores; at low levels it is also used as a preservative.
